buyback(uint256,uint256).details: `minAmountOut` is supplied by the caller, unlike the rebalance path      where slippage is the guard's parameter rather than the keeper's.      The difference is not an oversight: rebalancing trades assets that      have Chainlink feeds, so a fair price can be asserted on-chain.      This token has no feed, and the pool's own spot price is worthless      as a reference because an attacker who sandwiches this transaction      moves that spot first -- the check would validate against the very      price being manipulated.      So the bound here is size, not price: `maxSpendPerCall` plus the      guard's cooldown put a ceiling on what a compromised keeper can      lose per unit time, and what it can lose is fee revenue rather      than anyone's principal. Set `maxSpendPerCall` accordingly.

params.maxSpend: Upper bound for this call, further capped by the balance        on hand and by `maxSpendPerCall`.
params.minAmountOut: Least the swap may return, enforced by SwapExecutor        on the amount actually received.

collect(address,uint256).details: Redeems through the vault's ordinary exit, so it is subject to the      same refusal to price a stale basket that protects depositors. The      fee stream waits rather than being valued on a bad price.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setBurnsSupply(bool).details: Deliberately not auto-detected. Whether the protocol reduces its own      supply is a claim the docs make to holders, so it is a decision the      owner records on-chain rather than a behaviour that changes silently      depending on what the token happens to implement.

setPool((address,address,uint24,int24,ad.details: Validated to be exactly this pair, in either order. A key naming      some other pool would send the whole fee stream into it.

setVault(address,bool).details: The vault's asset must match what this contract spends, or `collect`      would fill it with a token no configured pool can trade.

sweep(address,address,uint256).details: This is not a back door onto depositor funds -- nothing here is      theirs. It is the same authority the owner already has by pointing      a vault's fee recipient somewhere else, made explicit.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

params.data: The data that was passed to the call to unlock

returns._0: Any data that you want to be returned from the unlock call

burnsSupply().notice: True to burn what is bought, false to send it to the graveyard.

buyback(uint256,uint256).notice: Spend stable on the protocol token and retire what is bought.

collect(address,uint256).notice: Redeem fee shares held by this contract for stable.

guard().notice: Contract permitted to run automation alongside the owner.

isVault(address).notice: Vaults whose fee shares this contract will redeem.

maxSpendPerCall().notice: Largest amount of stable a single buyback may spend.

pool().notice: The v4 pool a buyback trades through. Owner-set, never inferred.

stable().notice: The asset fees are denominated in, and what buybacks spend.

sweep(address,address,uint256).notice: Recover anything sitting here, including an in-kind redemption         that arrived as basket tokens rather than stable.

token().notice: The protocol token being bought and retired.

totalRetired().notice: Cumulative token amount retired by this contract, either way.

unlockCallback(bytes).notice: Called by the pool manager on `msg.sender` when the manager is unlocked
